requirement: The system shall transport at least 5,000 kg of cargo per round trip from a GTO-class staging orbit to the Earth–Moon NRHO.
The system shall return up to 500 kg of cargo per round trip from NRHO to the staging orbit.
The system shall provide a velocity change of at least 2.64 km/s per leg at the maximum outbound mass (13.4 t).
The system shall complete a round trip, including 60 days of end operations, in no more than 1.66 years.
The system shall have a design life of 15 years and perform at least 9 round trips.
The system shall be compatible with an Ariane 64 launch to a GTO-class orbit, with a launch mass not exceeding 11,500 kg.
The system shall provide a total thrust of at least 1.46 N at a specific impulse of at least 2,100 s.
The system shall store at least 3,400 kg of usable xenon.

requirement: The system shall accept in-orbit replenishment of at least 2,550 kg of xenon per round trip.
The system shall process at least 22.8 t of xenon over its design life.
The system shall supply at least 25 kW to the electric propulsion at end of life, in addition to platform loads.
The system shall keep all platform functions powered through eclipses of up to 2.5 h; longer eclipses are excluded by trajectory design.

requirement: The system shall meet its end-of-life performance after the total ionising dose of its life (dose TBD).
The system shall autonomously rendezvous with and capture a cargo in the staging orbit.
The system shall approach and dock with the lunar orbit destination only after receiving approach clearance.
The system shall provide one standard docking interface for cargo, destination and propellant supplier (standard TBD, IBDM-compatible TBC).
The system shall release cargo with a separation velocity of no more than TBD.
The system shall receive telecommands and transmit telemetry at all ranges up to 450,000 km.
The system shall determine its orbit and attitude autonomously during transfer (accuracy TBD).
On detecting a failure, the system shall autonomously enter a power-positive, thermally safe mode and remain in it for at least TBD days without ground contact.
The system shall execute a collision-avoidance manoeuvre within TBD hours of a ground command.
The system shall keep at all times a propellant reserve sufficient for its end-of-life disposal (delta-v TBD).
At end of life the system shall perform a heliocentric disposal via lunar flyby or a controlled lunar impact, and passivate all stored energy.
The electric propulsion, power processing, solar arrays, GNC software and docking and refuelling interfaces shall be sourced from European industry.
The system shall capture the cargo and its propellant module as one stack in a single rendezvous per round trip.
The system shall release the empty propellant module into an orbit that meets the applicable debris rules (decay time TBD).
